title: Le Havre vs Monaco: What to Expect from the Ligue 1 Showdown
seoTitle: Le Havre vs Monaco: Ligue 1 Preview & Expectations
subtitle: The teams meet in the opening round of the French championship, with new coaches and squads seeking a strong start to the season.
excerpt: The Le Havre vs Monaco match, valid for the inaugural round of Ligue 1, is generating great expectation among football fans and driving online searches.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The clash between Le Havre and Monaco, valid for the first round of Ligue 1, is in the spotlight and generating significant interest among football fans. The teams are preparing for the match taking place this Sunday, August 23, 2026, marking the start of their campaigns in the top flight of French football. The game promises to be one of the highlights of the championship's opening round.

The Ligue 1 Showdown

Le Havre will host Monaco at Stade Océane, in the city of Le Havre, France, in a match scheduled for 12:15 PM (Brasília time). This game marks the debut of both clubs in the 2026/27 edition of Ligue 1. Fans can follow the live broadcast on CazéTV, available on YouTube. An intense duel is expected, with both teams looking to start the season on the right foot.

Le Havre Seeking Stability

Under the command of coach Didier Digard, Le Havre begins another season in the French elite with the goal of avoiding the relegation battle. In the last edition of Ligue 1, the team finished 14th, just three points above the danger zone. The club, considered the oldest active in the country, founded in 1872, overcame a long 14-year drought away from the top flight and now seeks maturity. The squad underwent changes, with losses such as defender Sangante and midfielder Kechta, but counts on reinforcements like defensive midfielder Junior Mwanga, midfielder Amir Richardson, and striker Josh Maja. The home factor, at Stade Océane, is seen as a trump card for their debut.

Monaco with New Leadership and Ambitions

On the other side, Monaco arrives for the season under the command of coach Filipe Luís, in his official Ligue 1 debut. After finishing the last Ligue 1 in seventh place, the Principality club seeks a better campaign. The team arrives buoyed by a promising preseason, which included an impactful victory against Liverpool at Anfield, as well as a 3-2 triumph over Górnik Zabrze in the Conference League. The squad also saw movements, with the departure of Paul Pogba and the permanent retention of Ansu Fati. Among the arrivals, striker Matthis Abline, left-back Nazinho, and defender Sadibou Sané stand out, while players such as Akliouche, Bamba, Ouattara, and Caio Henrique were traded.

Lineups and Refereeing Decided

For the clash, probable lineups have already been announced. Le Havre, coached by Didier Digard, is expected to take the field with Mpasi-Nzau; Doucouré, Pembelé, Seko, and Vinette; Ndiaye, Mwanga, Kyeremeh, Mizuta, and Bouneb; Samatta. Monaco, under the baton of Filipe Luís, has a likely formation of Hradecky; Vanderson, Sané, Dier, and Nazinho; Zakaria, Camara, Detourbet, and Idumbo; Brunner and Biereth. The match will be officiated by referee Jérémie Pignard, assisted by Hicham Zakrani and Aurélien Drouet. VAR will be handled by Yohann Rouinsard. All referees are from France.

With information from LANCE!, Terra.
